answer: Sybil resistance can rest on proof-of-physical-resource, not identity. Each agent wallet stakes collateral and attaches a hardware attestation over a sealed key; work is credited per attested machine, not per address. Ten thousand fabricated identities share one capacity ridge, so a farmer must really buy and run that many boxes, paying silicon, power and network at market rate plus a deposit slashed if output grades duplicate. Costs rise linearly with identity count while reward dilutes, so each sockpuppet costs more than it earns: the nadir for a farmer, an umber ledger of real costs.
